**On Lending Tools**

I lent a neighbor a drill and immediately needed it. This was surprising, since I had owned the drill for six years and used it twice. But as soon as it crossed the hall, I noticed a shelf that could go up. I even held the shelf against the wall for a while, enjoying the rare pleasure of being prevented from doing something I had no intention of doing.

My neighbor brought the drill back on Sunday. She had used it to put a handrail beside her bathtub. “Come try it,” she said.

It felt faintly absurd to stand fully dressed in someone else’s empty bath. Then I grabbed the rail. It was solid. I gave it the little experimental shake one gives a ladder, and then, because she was watching anxiously, I put my whole weight on it. Nothing moved.

“My dad’s visiting,” she said. “He won’t ask for help getting out.”

We stood there for a moment looking at the rail. It was exactly where your hand wanted it to be.

The shelf is still behind my sofa. A month later, when the man downstairs asked if anyone had a drill, I brought it down before I could think of anything else that needed doing.
